cal-platform.summary: The platform I am building for Calisthenics Alliance, Portugal's national Endurance league. It handles registrations, divisions, 1v1 battles, judging, rankings, results, and the admin work around an event.
cal-platform.impact: It is being used to support a real competition organization and make the event days easier to run for the organizers and judges.
cal-platform.organization: Built for Calisthenics Alliance, a league created by Associação B.W.C.R. - Clube de Calistenia das Caldas da Rainha, together with clubs, athletes, and organizations from the Portuguese calisthenics community.
cal-platform.overview: CAL is built around an Open CAL, four regular rounds, and a Grand Final. I am building the platform around that format, from registration and division assignment to battle generation, judging, rankings, and results. The services can run on the venue's local network, which keeps the setup practical on the day.
contributions: Built the Go services around CAL's seasons, categories, divisions, athletes, battles, judging, rankings, and results.
Created the admin screens for registrations, division assignment, battle generation, and event setup.
Connected the platform to the venue's local network and set up the Docker services needed for an event.
Built the workflows that the organization and judges use during CAL events.

cal-judge.summary: A native Android app I am building for Calisthenics Alliance judges. It connects to the CAL event platform and supports battles, routines, timers, and judging on site.
cal-judge.impact: It gives the judges a focused tool for the competition day and keeps their work connected to the same event system used by the organization.
cal-judge.organization: Built for Calisthenics Alliance, the Portuguese endurance league created by Associação B.W.C.R. - Clube de Calistenia das Caldas da Rainha with the wider calisthenics community.
cal-judge.overview: The app covers the judging side of CAL, where athletes compete in 1v1 battles within categories and divisions under the same criteria from the National Judging Committee. I am keeping the workflow close to what judges need at the venue: select a battle, follow the routine, record each completed repetition, and adjust the count up or down when needed so they can keep track of the athlete's progress through the CAL API. A repetition is one complete execution of an exercise.
contributions: Set up the Kotlin Multiplatform project, Android toolchain, build workflow, and emulator and release APK testing.
Built the screens for battle selection, judging, timers, set and repetition progress, and settings.
Connected the app to the API and the local Wi-Fi network used at the venue.
Kept the controls native to Android, including hardware volume-button input, while leaving room for a future native iOS app.
